Bierun Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bieruń, Poland

Not demolished. Established in 1778, this cemetery holds 47 preserved stelae inscribed in both German and Hebrew, crafted by named stonemasons from Gliwice, Katowice, and Oświęcim — the oldest identified, from 1818, made of sandstone. Bieruń's kehilla, formally legalized in 1812, declined sharply after a new railway bypassed the town, falling from 364 members in 1840 to just 157 by 1910; most of the remaining, more German-culturally aligned Jews left after the town's 1921 incorporation into Poland, leaving only a dozen or so by 1939, who were later transferred to the Będzin and Sosnowiec ghettos and deported to Auschwitz-Birkenau. The cemetery has been carefully restored in recent decades, including a 1980s gate decorated with a menorah and, more recently, a renovated wall, trimmed greenery, and a restored historical path layout.
